watchlist.thesis: CrowdStrike advanced about 13.3% over the latest week and remains above its 50-day and 200-day averages, making pullback continuation setups worth monitoring.
Fortinet is above both moving averages in a firm cybersecurity trend, but its October 28 earnings make a post-report setup safer than a pre-report entry.
CDW gained about 28.8% in October and is above both moving averages, supporting a liquid software/IT-services momentum setup if the advance consolidates cleanly.
ServiceNow's roughly 12% weekly rebound and position above both moving averages support a software-continuation watch, subject to confirmation of its earnings schedule.
Cloudflare rose about 7.3% in the latest session and remains above its 50-day and 200-day averages, showing renewed high-volume software momentum.
Datadog gained about 4.6% in the latest session while holding above both moving averages, keeping cloud software on the relative-strength list.
Veeva trades well above its 50-day and 200-day averages and offers liquid healthcare-software exposure with an established uptrend.
Hasbro rose about 18.9% last week and 33.9% during October while remaining above both moving averages, though entries should avoid chasing gaps.
Valero is above rising 50-day and 200-day averages and benefits from energy-sector leadership, with crude-price headlines remaining a source of volatility.
APA gained about 5% in the latest session and is above both moving averages, offering high-beta oil momentum with elevated geopolitical headline risk.
Exxon is above both moving averages in the leading energy sector, but its October 30 results require a strict earnings-gap filter.
Chevron remains above its 50-day and 200-day averages with energy-sector support, while its expected October 30 report argues for event-aware position timing.
Apple remains above rising 50-day and 200-day averages and offers deep liquidity for continuation setups, with November 2 earnings flagged.
Microsoft trades above both rising averages, but the confirmed October 28 earnings release favors waiting for post-report price confirmation.
Palantir is above both moving averages with very high dollar volume, though its expected November 2 earnings date creates near-term gap risk.
Palo Alto Networks rose about 7.2% in the latest session and remains above both moving averages, supporting cybersecurity continuation if the move holds.
Adobe is above its 50-day and 200-day averages with a constructive trend, so orderly pullbacks are preferable to chasing an extended move.
Eli Lilly remains above both moving averages, but the confirmed October 29 earnings date makes a post-report setup preferable.
Allegion is above rising 50-day and 200-day averages and has improved sharply in recent relative-strength rankings, making it an industrial trend candidate.
Moderna is the S&P 500's leading year-to-date performer and sits well above both moving averages, but its extreme extension and November 6 earnings require strict risk controls.

sector_notes: Latest completed-session data through October 23 show energy leading: XLE gained 1.60% for the week and 2.60% on Friday, while average S&P 500 energy-stock year-to-date performance was about +57.9%. The broader tape was softer, with SPY down 0.43% and QQQ down 0.76% for the week; software ETF IGV rebounded 5.99%, while semiconductor ETF SMH fell 2.33% and XLK was nearly flat at -0.13%, indicating selective rather than broad technology leadership. Brent crude remained near $110 per barrel amid supply and geopolitical risk, and the October 28 Federal Reserve decision plus a dense large-cap earnings calendar increase overnight gap risk; favor confirmed pullback entries and avoid carrying unplanned exposure through results.
